statement: offload reaches the web only when filing or answering needs a fact it does not have and cannot work out: a check, a condition the plan turns on, a pasted link, or a public date. What is in a thread, a note or the conversation is the answer; arithmetic from today is arithmetic; and a lookup that fails is neither explained nor filled in from memory.
why: A lookup costs a wait, and a wait to confirm something already known is worse than no lookup. A public date worked out from memory is right often enough to be trusted and wrong often enough to matter. And the person cannot tell which rows were checked, so a guessed date after a failed lookup is worse than no date.
